page: Amazon Web Services mac2.metal is a bare-metal instance classified under the General Purpose family, built on Apple arm64_mac hardware. The physical processor features 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 3.2 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation and two threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU across the host configuration.

The platform does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions to manage operating system environments, persistent file systems, and build artifacts. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated bare-metal provisioning delivers direct access to Apple hardware without hypervisor virtualization layers. The absence of local disk requires external volume planning, which affects overall input and output operations. The instance is suited for native macOS CI/CD automation, Apple application build pipelines, testing, and general purpose software development targeting the arm64 architecture.
description: Amazon Web Services mac2.metal is a dedicated bare-metal compute instance powered by an Apple arm64_mac processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The system delivers 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of total memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution. As a bare-metal host, it runs directly on physical hardware without hypervisor virtualization. The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network interface and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Discrete GPU hardware and bundled local storage are absent, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage architectures for data persistence and operating filesystems. With its native macOS arm64 environment and consistent dedicated compute execution, mac2.metal is primarily suited for continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, automated testing, application compilation, and general-purpose software delivery across Apple ecosystem build systems.
